paper_title: Facile Benzylic Alkylation of Arenes with Alcohols by Catalysis with Spirocyclic NHC IrIII Pincer Complex

knowledge_points.content: The catalyst SNIr-H is a spirocyclic N-heterocyclic carbene (SNHC)-based CCC pincer iridium(III) complex designed to facilitate the borrowing hydrogen alkylation of unactivated arenes.
knowledge_points.evidence: Due to the successful C-H silylation and olefin isomerization reactions that were catalyzed by our recently developed spirocyclic N-heterocyclic carbene (SNHC)-based IrIII CCC pincer complexes (SNIr-Cl)... Once the stable IrIII-H complex (SNIr-H) had been isolated, we began investigating the possible formation of IrIII dihydride.

knowledge_points.content: The synthesis of indeno[2,1-a]indene, a template for functional material molecules, was achieved in a 63% yield at a 1 mmol scale using indene and bromobenzyl alcohol via the SNIr-H catalyzed alkylation followed by Herrmann-Beller catalysis.
knowledge_points.evidence: Under similar conditions, compound 11 could be easily prepared in 63% yield at a 1 mmol scale using 1a and bromobenzyl alcohol 10; compound 11 was further converted to indeno[2,1-a] indene 12 via the Herrmann-Beller catalysis and is a versatile template for functional material molecules.

knowledge_points.content: The SNIr-H catalyzed benzylic alkylation of xanthene with benzyl alcohol achieved a maximum isolated yield of 89% for the product 7a.
knowledge_points.evidence: The reaction of xanthene (6a) and benzyl alcohol furnished the alkylation product 7a... the yield of 7a increased to 85% [later 89% in Table 4] in the presence of Cat A (5 mol%), KOtBu (1.5 equiv), and 18-crown-6 (1.0 equiv) at 140 °C.

knowledge_points.content: The hemilabile nature of the CCC pincer iridium complex provides sufficient coordination space around the metal center to activate sterically hindered, unactivated tetrasubstituted olefin intermediates.
knowledge_points.evidence: Furthermore, we envision that the hemilabile nature of the pincer complex may provide sufficient space around the metal center, thereby enabling the coordination/activation of the sterically hindered olefin intermediates.

knowledge_points.content: In the alkylation of substituted indenes, electron-donating groups (e.g., -Me, -OMe) on the aryl ring lead to higher yields (78-85%) compared to electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., -Br, -F), which result in lower yields (51-75%).
knowledge_points.evidence: The results indicated that using electron-donating groups (5e, 5f, 5h, 5k), as substituents, led to higher yields than those obtained when the substituents were electron-withdrawing groups (5g, 5i, 5j).

knowledge_points.content: The borrowing hydrogen (BH) strategy enables atom-economical alkylation using alcohols as the alkylating agent, producing water as the sole byproduct through a sequence of metal-catalyzed dehydrogenation, condensation, and hydrogenation.
knowledge_points.evidence: The BH strategy uses readily available alcohols, is an atom-economical and green alkylation method, and water is the only byproduct. A metal-catalyzed dehydrogenation, condensation, and hydrogenation sequence could realize the alkylation.

knowledge_points.content: Optimal reaction conditions for the C3-alkylation of indenes involve 1.5 equivalents of alcohol, 15 mol% of KOtBu base, and 1 mol% of the SNIr-H catalyst in toluene at 100 °C for 10 hours.
knowledge_points.evidence: The isolated yield of 3a increased to 85% upon increasing the loading of 2a and KOtBu to 1.5 equiv and 15 mol%, respectively (entry 15). Thus, the optimal condition was chosen as 2a (1.5 equiv) and KOtBu (15 mol%).

knowledge_points.content: For the alkylation of relatively inert sp3 C-H bonds in arenes like xanthene or thioxanthene, the addition of 1.0 equivalent of 18-crown-6 and an increased temperature of 140 °C are required to improve yields.
knowledge_points.evidence: Fortunately, the yield of 7a increased to 85% in the presence of Cat A (5 mol%), KOtBu (1.5 equiv), and 18-crown-6 (1.0 equiv) at 140 °C. These conditions were used for the reactions of the S- or N-containing cyclic substrates (7b-7e).

knowledge_points.content: Deuterium-labeling experiments using alcohol-D confirmed the mechanism by showing 84% deuterium retention at the C1 position of the alcohol-generated chain and 7% incorporation at the sp3 C1 of indene.
knowledge_points.evidence: Deuterium-labeling experiments were performed... compound 3a-D was isolated in 74% yield; with 7% deuterium being incorporated at the sp3 C1 of indene and 84% retained at C1 of the alcohol-generated chain.

knowledge_points.content: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were utilized to propose a catalytic cycle involving a hemilabile IrIII dihydride intermediate that selectively inserts into the exo double bond of a 1,3-diene intermediate.
knowledge_points.evidence: A hemilabile IrIII dihydride intermediate was proposed based on control experiments and previous density functional theory (DFT) calculations for the borrowing hydrogen mechanism... The selective migratory insertion of the Ir-hydride bond to the exo double bond is favored.

knowledge_points.content: The SNIr-H catalyst enables the synthesis of alkylated fluorene derivatives (5l-5o), which are widely applied in functional materials and optoelectronics.
knowledge_points.evidence: In addition to indenes, we also studied the alkylation of fluorenes because of their wide application in functional materials. Fluorene and its derivatives reacted successfully, affording the expected products (5l-5o) in high yields.
